candidate.title: TIVA
candidate.scope: TIVA (Transcriptome in vivo analysis), the assigned middle row of the Illumina schematic, interpreted as the caged, CPP-delivered poly-U TIVA-tag implementation described by Lovatt et al. (2014). The drawn architecture spans tag loading, CPP release, photoactivation, intracellular mRNA hybridization, streptavidin-bead capture and mRNA recovery. The CirSeq row above, PAIR row below and adjacent PAIR chemical structure are separate context, not alternatives or components of TIVA. The Whole-genome RNA icon is a target-context illustration, not a material transfer into tag synthesis. No unshown amplification or library-preparation operations are added to the graph.

states.label: Extracellular, CPP-conjugated caged TIVA-tag
features: A hairpin pairs a biotin-bearing, Cy3-labeled poly-U capture segment with poly-A blocking segments; two PL symbols denote photocleavable linkers.
The lower segment carries Cy5 and a CPP connected through a disulfide bond (-S-S-); the legend expands CPP as Cell-penetrating peptide.

The primary implementation identifies the capture segment as an 18-mer 2′-fluoro RNA poly-U and the blockers as two 7-mer 2′-O-methyl RNA poly-A segments. These modifications distinguish capture affinity and light-dependent unmasking.
Cy3 and Cy5 form a monitoring FRET pair. Biotin is the affinity handle; these labels do not encode a transcript sequence or cell barcode.
The primary implementation uses a (D-Arg)9 delivery CPP; delivery performance is not assumed to generalize to every cell type or CPP.

states.label: Recovered mRNA from the selected single cell
features: The depicted endpoint is a magenta line labeled mRNA from single cell; no sequencing library, adapters or sequencing reads are drawn.
The primary figure describes elution of mRNA for amplification. The bare line denotes the recovered RNA fraction and does not establish the complete chemical composition of the eluate.

Paper-only downstream interface: recovered mRNA is linearly amplified by in vitro transcription to aRNA, which supplies Tru-Seq library construction and Illumina sequencing. These unshown operations are not graph nodes.

The resulting library represents sequences derived from the captured endogenous polyadenylated transcripts of the illuminated cell. The capture tag supplies affinity and spatial selection rather than the transcriptome sequence readout. Capture and downstream amplification do not establish unbiased total-RNA recovery or uniform full-length coverage.
